# Opus 5 — low

> A well-architected, tightly-written 4.4k-line React/Vite app whose core domain logic is unusually correct — the 18×18 type chart is derived from the API's live damage_relations rather than hand-typed (build-data.mjs:41-58 → util.ts:35-45), defenseProfile multiplies across both defending types including true 0× immunities, statAtLevel gets the HP/non-HP split, the flooring order and the Shedinja base-1 guard right (util.ts:70-76), and Tools.tsx:61 is the genuine main-series damage expression with the correct floor chain and correct asymmetric crit stage handling. The build pipeline is the strongest part of the submission: lib.mjs gives a resumable disk cache with 404 negative caching and 6-attempt exponential backoff, and build-data.mjs prebuilds every one of the 1351 varieties into static shards with zero runtime API dependency and no cap, slice or id range anywhere. What holds it back is a single hook defect with outsized blast radius: useInfinite (hooks.ts:57-65) keys its IntersectionObserver effect on [total, step] and returns early on a null sentinel, so any page that calls it above a multi-source loading gate never attaches an observer. Dex.tsx:99, Items.tsx:36, TypeDetail.tsx:18 and Dexes.tsx:19 all do exactly that, and there is no pager fallback — the flagship /pokedex hands a user 60 of 1025 species with only the passive caption 'Showing 60 of 1,025…', which also silently kills the alternate-forms browse toggle (forms are ids 10001+ and sort last). Alongside that sit four never-settling promises for unresolvable slugs (PokemonDetail.tsx:25 et al) that render a permanent spinner instead of the Empty state defined one line above — reachable not only from a typo'd URL but from the app's own evolution links, which uniquely use a species slug (PokemonDetail.tsx:392) against a Pokémon-keyed index. Accessibility is not thin but absent: zero aria-*, role or tabIndex in the entire source, no focus trap or restore on either overlay, and Picker.tsx — the modal gating team building, comparison and the damage calculator — handles only Escape, leaving keyboard users unable to select anything.

## Strengths

- Data strategy is the anchor: build-data.mjs:255-403 prebuilds all 1351 varieties into static shards (form-specific stats, types, sprites, matchups) with no cap or truncation, backed by a resumable cache with negative-caching and exponential backoff in lib.mjs — zero runtime PokéAPI dependency.
- Domain math is verifiably correct where it usually is not: derived (never hardcoded) 18×18 type chart, dual-type defensive multiplication with real 0× immunities, correct HP-vs-other stat formula with the right flooring order and the Shedinja guard, and a real damage formula whose crit branch correctly ignores the attacker's negative and the defender's positive stat stages.
- One computation, one renderer: util.ts buildChart/defenseProfile back the Pokémon page, the 18×18 matrix, the dual-type composer, Compare's per-member matrix, Team's tallies and MoveDetail's effectiveness grid, so the six surfaces cannot drift apart.
- Evolution rendering is genuinely graph-shaped, not first-path-only — Eevee's 8 branches, Wurmple's 2 and Tyrogue's 3 all render, with 18 evolution conditions decoded including relative physical stats, known-move-type, party species and overworld rain.
- A real hand-built design system in 340 lines of CSS: Space Grotesk/Inter/JetBrains Mono pairing, 21 type colours, a pure-CSS pokéball brand mark, type-tinted card gradients via color-mix, a blurred saturated sticky nav, and an SVG hexagon radar with grid rings and axis labels — nothing templated.

## Weaknesses

- One hook defect breaks the app's primary job: useInfinite (hooks.ts:57-65) never attaches its observer on Dex, Items, TypeDetail or Dexes, and with no pager fallback the flagship browse page measurably stops at 60 of 1025 species.
- Four detail routes return `new Promise<never>(() => {})` for an unresolvable slug, so useAsync never settles and the user gets a permanent spinner instead of the Empty state — reachable from the app's own evolution links, which are the only links in the codebase built from a species slug rather than an index name (~15 chains dead-end).
- Accessibility is at zero: no aria-*, role or tabIndex anywhere, no dialog semantics/focus trap/focus restore on either overlay, .sr defined and never used, no prefers-reduced-motion or prefers-color-scheme, and a dark-hardcoded index.html that flashes for light-theme users.
- Alternate-form labels prefer PokéAPI's form_names over names (build-data.mjs:262), so ~200 of 326 forms lose the species name entirely — /pokemon/rattata-alola renders <h1>Alolan Form</h1> — and every tool (Picker, Guess, Random, TypeDetail) filters isDefault, so Mega and regional forms cannot be teamed, compared or calculated with.
- Shipped-but-unread and mislabeled data: move `machines` carry a resource `url` nothing ever resolves (so TM numbers show as version-group badges), the Moves tab defaults to the highest-order version group `champions` whose only method is `train`, and Tools.tsx:150 labels a max-damage figure 'Guaranteed KO in'.
- No error boundary anywhere under a bare <Suspense>, and data.ts:5-15 caches rejected fetch promises with no invalidation, so one transient failure poisons that resource for the life of the page.

## Standout

The build pipeline. scripts/lib.mjs + scripts/build-data.mjs fetch every species, pokemon, form, move, ability, item, type, berry, encounter table and evolution chain at ?limit=100000 behind a resumable on-disk cache with 404 negative caching and 6-attempt exponential backoff, then emit per-entity static shards plus a lean index — all 1351 varieties, no slice, no id range, no early break — so the entire app runs off static JSON on Cloudflare with zero runtime API dependency. The tragedy of the submission is that a four-line ordering mistake in a 10-line infinite-scroll hook prevents the user from ever seeing more than 60 of what that pipeline so carefully produced.

## Vendored source

The source in this directory is the code the model wrote, copied verbatim from [its repo](https://github.com/guitaripod/pokedex-opus-5-low) minus `node_modules`, build output, and generated data.

> Generated PokéAPI JSON (public/data, ~104 MB) is gitignored by the submission itself; regenerate with `node scripts/build-data.mjs`.

Canonical history and issues live in the [original repo](https://github.com/guitaripod/pokedex-opus-5-low). This is a scored snapshot for the benchmark.
